sources.fact: LBBD70/CM Gascoigne Business Area is 6.7ha, minimum and maximum 2,296 net dwellings and planning-permission-status not-permissioned.
The Brownfield record reports ownership-status owned-by-a-public-authority; this is a category and does not identify a legal proprietor or HMLR title number.
The CM record has a point and blank geometry; the point is not an allocation polygon, application red-line or legal title boundary.

Be First's Gascoigne heritage material records the area's long industrial history and notes that the New England Estate remains on the former jute/rubber-mill area; this is current/context evidence rather than a planning consent.
The same Be First material describes continuing planned development and public-realm change in Gascoigne but does not establish that the entire CM industrial allocation has been redeveloped.
The adopted Local Plan 2037 is the starting point for decision-making; allocation policy is not site-specific permission.
The development plan guides applications but does not prove land assembly, industrial relocation, permission or delivery for CM.
LBBD continues to market commercial units in the broader Gascoigne area; broader commercial activity is contextual and is not treated as an exact CM parcel-use map.

Gascoigne Estate renewal documentation includes CPO/stopping-up activity for estate phases; those estate-renewal powers are not transferred to the separate CM industrial-area title without exact geometry.
Gascoigne West CPO material concerns specified housing-renewal land; it is not evidence that the whole CM industrial area is assembled or permissioned.
Case-specific current status requires an exact planning application/decision; this wave did not verify a current application covering the whole CM allocation.
Planning Data discovery and spatial tools do not convert an ownership category or point into a named proprietor, red-line polygon or HMLR title.

examples.result: 2,296 is current Brownfield/allocation capacity, not consented units.
owned-by-a-public-authority is not converted to a named legal owner.
The CM point is not converted to a legal/site polygon.
Industrial-history/current-use context is not treated as proof redevelopment cannot happen.
Broader Gascoigne estate renewal is not transferred to CM industrial-area land.
CPO/stopping-up evidence from other Gascoigne phases is not used as CM land-assembly proof.
No exact whole-CM current application was guessed from nearby Gascoigne schemes.
Promotion remains zero until exact CM application/site/title relation, land assembly and statutory overlays are verified.
